overview: ANSE is a model-aware noise selection framework for video diffusion models that uses BANSA (Bayesian Active Noise Selection via Attention), an uncertainty-based acquisition function measuring entropy disagreement across stochastic attention samples, to select initial noise seeds yielding more confident and consistent generation results.

modules.name: Configuration Management
modules.description: Centralized YAML/JSON-based configuration for all experiment hyperparameters including noise pool size, ensemble size K, Bernoulli masking probability, layer truncation threshold, model backbones, evaluation protocols, and ablation study variants, with support for configuration inheritance and experiment tracking.

modules.name: Attention Map Extraction
modules.description: Hook-based module that intercepts and extracts attention maps (query-key softmax outputs) from specified layers of video diffusion denoising networks during forward passes, supporting both self-attention and cross-attention types across heterogeneous architectures (U-Net, MMDiT), with row-stochastic normalization guarantee.

modules.name: Bernoulli Mask Sampler
modules.description: Generates i.i.d. binary masks from Bernoulli distribution for stochastic attention perturbation, applies element-wise masking to attention maps, and re-normalizes masked rows to valid probability distributions, enabling multiple stochastic attention samples from a single forward pass.

modules.name: BANSA Score Computation
modules.description: Core acquisition function implementing the BALD-style formulation adapted to attention space: computes the difference between the entropy of the mean attention map and the mean of individual attention map entropies across K stochastic samples, with proof-verified zero condition when all samples are identical, supporting both full and Bernoulli-masked approximations.

modules.name: Layer Selection via Cumulative Correlation
modules.description: Implements the correlation-based layer truncation procedure: computes per-layer BANSA scores, calculates cumulative averages up to each depth, measures Pearson correlation between truncated and full-layer scores across a calibration set of prompts and seeds, and identifies the minimal depth d* where correlation exceeds the threshold.

modules.name: Noise Pool Generator
modules.description: Generates and manages a pool of M candidate Gaussian noise seeds for a given latent shape, supporting both standard sampling and deterministic seeding for reproducibility, with optional pre-filtering or diversity-aware sampling strategies.

modules.name: ANSE Pipeline Orchestrator
modules.description: End-to-end workflow controller that coordinates the full noise selection pipeline: generates noise pool, extracts Bernoulli-masked attention from early denoising steps at truncated layers, computes BANSA scores for each candidate, selects the seed with minimum score, and invokes the video generation sampling process with the selected seed.

modules.name: Video Diffusion Backbone Wrappers
modules.description: Unified interface layer wrapping diverse T2V diffusion models (AnimateDiff, CogVideoX-2B/5B, Wan2.1, HunyuanVideo, IPOC-2B) with standardized APIs for single-step denoising, attention map access, latent space operations, and full video sampling, handling architecture-specific differences in temporal modules and attention structures.

modules.name: VBench Evaluation Pipeline
modules.description: Integrates the VBench benchmark evaluation protocol computing Quality Score (weighted average of subject/background consistency, temporal flickering, motion smoothness, aesthetic/imaging quality, dynamic degree) and Semantic Score (object class, multiple objects, color, spatial relationship, scene, temporal/appearance style, overall consistency, human action), with GPT-4o augmented prompts for long-video assessment.

modules.name: FVMD Metric Computation
modules.description: Implements the Fréchet Video Motion Distance metric for evaluating motion consistency by computing distributional distance between generated and reference video motion features, applied on MSR-VTT dataset with sampled text prompts and real video references.

modules.name: Ablation Study Framework
modules.description: Systematic ablation infrastructure supporting controlled experiments: acquisition function comparison (Random, Entropy, BANSA-Dropout, BANSA-Bernoulli), ensemble size K sweep, noise pool size M sweep, reversed BANSA criterion, Bernoulli probability p sensitivity, temporal scope analysis (1-step vs multi-step), attention space disentanglement (self vs cross), CFG scale interaction, equivalent compute budget comparison, and full-layer vs truncated score comparison.

modules.name: Noise Behavior Analysis
modules.description: Analytical module for cross-prompt and intra-prompt noise behavior studies: cross-prompt evaluation transfers high-BANSA seeds between prompts to demonstrate prompt-dependent effectiveness; intra-prompt analysis computes pairwise Euclidean distances between attention maps from high vs low BANSA seeds to measure attention consistency.

modules.name: Latent Dynamics Analysis
modules.description: Implements latent trajectory analysis using Butterworth low-pass filtering to isolate structural components, computing Latent Trajectory Variation (temporal stability of low-frequency structure) and Intra-frame Variance (spatial expressiveness within frames) across full denoising trajectories for high and low BANSA seeds.

modules.name: Statistical Validation Module
modules.description: Computes 95% confidence intervals over multiple independent evaluation runs using random subsets, performs Pearson correlation analysis between BANSA scores and quality metrics, and validates statistical significance of improvements across all VBench dimensions and backbones.

modules.name: User Study Evaluation
modules.description: Side-by-side human preference evaluation infrastructure: randomized pairing of baseline and ANSE-generated videos, blind evaluation protocol with multiple independent evaluators, assessing Video Quality (stability and visual appeal) and Prompt Alignment (text-video semantic fidelity), with aggregated preference statistics.

modules.name: Visualization and Reporting
modules.description: Generates attention map visualizations, BANSA score vs. quality correlation scatter plots, cumulative correlation curves for layer selection, qualitative comparison grids across backbones, automated LaTeX tables for VBench/FVMD results with confidence intervals, and failure case analysis visualizations.
